verdict.rationale: React's own docs say it can stream HTML on the server while data is still being fetched, progressively filling in content before any JavaScript loads. It also renders on the server via Node, and `hydrateRoot` attaches interactivity to HTML generated by `react-dom/server`. Missing for 10: reference-level docs for the streaming server APIs themselves, evidence of progressive/selective hydration speeding up time-to-interactive, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
